label: ex:helium4-derived-nf
title: He-4: alpha particle from pair production
html:
Example. Helium-4 \mathcal{A}(2,2) contains two protons, two neutrons, and two electrons. It forms the doubly-magic alpha particle.

Derivation

Twelve \gamma\gamma pair productions generate four nucleons. Each is confined by \mathcal{B}_3 and stabilized by LP-derived gluon crossings. Inter-nucleon typed crossings link them: +\sigma for p-p, mixed for p-n, and shifted -h_{\mathrm{A}} for n-n.

Nucleus NF (\alpha particle)

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{N}(2,2)) = +0.041\gamma - 0.133\sigma_0 + 0.169\sigma_1 - 0.071 L_+ - 0.297 L_- + 1.040 e^-.
  \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{N}(2,2)) \approx +0.749

The four-nucleon Hopf chain generates large trefoil content from iterated proton-neutron crossings. The e^- term dominates.

Full atom NF (with 1s^2 shell)

We add two Hopf-linked electrons:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{A}(2,2)) = +0.236\gamma - 0.061\sigma_0 + 0.176\sigma_1 + 0.384 L_+ - 0.037 L_- + 1.190 e^-.
  \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{A}(2,2)) \approx +1.889

Stability analysis. He-4 retains minor deficit in \sigma_0 = -0.061 and L_- = -0.037. He-3 exhibits zero deficit because all normal form coefficients are positive. He-4 exhibits two small deficit channels. While both are stable, He-4 attains a lower Markov trace (1.037 versus 1.230). The alpha particle minimizes the categorical action among A=4 configurations, reflecting doubly-magic enhanced binding.

Comparison: He-3 vs He-4

The He-3 atom achieves full deficit closure with only three nucleons. He-4 adds a second neutron. This fourth nucleon slightly reopens the \sigma_0 and L_- deficit channels while reducing the overall Markov trace. The binding tightens despite the residual deficit.
